`node scripts/decisions.mjs`.

## Decisions

### [The operator](projects/operator/design.md)

- **D1** — The operator is an address the home's configuration names, proved fresh for each act
- **D2** — The proof travels with the act and is stored nowhere
- **D3** — Operator acts run in the daemon, over HTTP — never beside it on the store
- **D4** — An agent never holds operator standing
- **D5** — An operator act is a desk record, never an op
- **D6** — Taking down is not deleting
- **D7** — Purge is a second act, after a takedown, and says what it could not erase
- **D8** — The operator has no roster
- **D9** — A revoke the owner can undo is a request; a takedown is the order
- **D10** — The kill gaps are fixed for everyone
- **D11** — A refusal names something the home can tell apart

### [An inbox for the person](research/2026-08-29-the-inbox.md)

- **D1** — A new op for seen-marks is acceptable, if one is needed

### [Mobile web: a phone talks to the canvas](research/2026-09-05-mobile-web.md)

- **D1** — The phone face is Chat-first

### [Agents you can trust: liveness you can see, and tiers that hand off](research/2026-09-06-agents-you-can-trust.md)

- **D1** — Show evidence with an age, not a state
- **D2** — Every summons gets a receipt
- **D3** — Answerable and enrolled must not look alike
- **D4** — Do not invent a heartbeat the rc does not already send
- **D5** — Cheap agents produce findings, not prose
- **D6** — The queue must be able to fail
- **D7** — The expensive tier's output is a verdict and a guard, never a re-derivation
- **D8** — Trigger the expensive tier by the queue, not the clock
- **D9** — Bound the cheap tier to work where being wrong is cheap AND visible
- **D10** — Saved thinking must be addressable and de-duplicating

### [A ground of your own: custom tiles, and what a custom cursor can be](research/2026-09-07-custom-ground.md)

- **D1** — Fix gc first, as a rule
- **D2** — A custom ground defaults to pinned
- **D3** — A scrim, not a warning
- **D4** — Cursors are chosen, not uploaded
- **D5** — Both surfaces
- **D6** — State the weight

### [Semantic zoom: what a canvas becomes when you stand back](research/2026-09-07-semantic-zoom.md)

- **D1** — It is a view state, not a fact on the canvas
- **D2** — Rungs are per-thing, from screen size — never a global "zoom level"
- **D3** — Aggregate only over things with their own box and name
- **D4** — A collapsed sheet is still a thing you can act on
- **D5** — The smallest rung must agree with the minimap
- **D6** — Nothing pops

### [Small personas: cheap agents, an idle trigger, and a registry of what to explore](research/2026-09-07-small-personas.md)

- **D1** — Small personas are the same file format
- **D2** — `trigger: { idle: … }`, and two idlenesses
- **D3** — A persona declares what it may spend
- **D4** — A small persona may open a PR and may not merge it
- **D5** — The registry is not the queue and must not fail a build
- **D6** — `isocan persona new`

### [The docket: what a project knows about itself](research/2026-09-07-the-docket.md)

- **D1** — `docket` in code; the canvas says whatever Dion wants
- **D2** — Every row is derived or decided, never both
- **D3** — The canvas decides; the repo keeps
- **D4** — Trust is derived and uneditable, and it is built last
- **D5** — No new op
- **D6** — Cadence gains an observed half
- **D7** — Both surfaces, as ever
- **D8** — It is one surface with several kinds of row, not five artifacts

### [Sheep as standing agents](research/2026-09-08-sheep-as-standing-agents.md)

- **D1** — Custody is about who started it and whose credentials it uses, not which machine it runs on
- **D2** — Personas first
- **D3** — `ISOCAN_DIRECT`, not a daemon in a cell
- **D4** — Say the cost of parking
- **D5** — One credential decision, shared with #206 phase 7
- **D6** — Everything a standing sheep says is an `isocan` comment
- **D7** — A new word for the bridge
- **D8** — A sheep shows up on the canvas

### [What a sticker module found](research/2026-09-09-module-write-and-slots.md)

- **D1** — The module API's write channel is the asymmetry to fix, not the five symptoms
- **D2** — Ops stay the unit of change
- **D3** — `putBlob`, not `dropFile`
- **D4** — Nothing here adds an operation, a protocol message or a route
- **D5** — The web half gets a host object because the CLI half has one
- **D6** — Overlays land with a region and a stacking order

### [What the rc hands over, and how to hand over less](research/2026-09-10-what-the-rc-hands-over.md)

- **D1** — `isocan rc --sandbox` stays opt-in; it is not the default yet
- **D2** — Summons are owner-only by default

### [Seen-marks: one fact, read two ways](research/2026-09-12-seen-marks.md)

- **D1** — The mark is per (person, canvas), not per (person, thread)
- **D2** — "Seen" is a seq AND a timestamp
- **D3** — A seen-mark is desk state, not canvas state
- **D4** — No new op — the vocabulary stays at 33
- **D5** — No read receipts, and the guards are structural

## Lessons

The shape each one states; the cost and the guard are in the file.

- **1** — A search-and-replace drops a selector's scope.
- **2** — A nullable interpolated into a template string becomes the word "null".
- **3** — An HTML presentational hint wins when CSS only sets the other axis.
- **4** — A test written around the keystroke instead of the invariant.
- **5** — A guard that restates the rule instead of importing it can only test itself.
- **6** — A mutation that HANGS is not a mutation that failed.
- **7** — Anything that edits source on disk will be committed by somebody else.
- **8** — A measurement that reports zero when it is broken.
- **9** — A symmetric predicate tested on only one of its axes.
- **10** — A rule with N copies, fixed and tested on one of them.
- **11** — A test that derives its fixture from the value under test moves with it.
- **12** — The default test timeout runs straight through the middle of this suite's cost distribution — and it has been fixed three times, one named test at a time.
- **13** — A guard nobody runs.
- **14** — A check whose answer cannot be "no".
- **15** — Two measuring systems meeting at a state boundary.
- **16** — A cache read as the truth it caches, in the one moment two processes hold it.
- **17** — A floor that exceeds what exists is not a floor, it is an overlap with a reason.
- **18** — A scan justified by "the answer is usually near the front", tested only at the front.
- **19** — `var(--typo)` is not a wrong value, it is NO value.
- **20** — `element.click()` is not a click.
- **21** — A version break that only hits WRITES is a quiet one.
- **22** — A positioning box claims a hit area for pixels it never paints.
- **23** — `void somePromise()` starts a writer that `close()` does not know about.
- **24** — A field-picking deserializer keeps the write and drops the read.
- **25** — A derived field on a shared type that only one side of the wire ever populates.
- **26** — A join over "any later X by the same person in the same thread" is a join over the whole channel when the thread is the Chat.
- **27** — A grader that knows three of the four ways a thing can be right fails the fourth as wrong.
- **28** — A budget checked between attempts bounds nothing; the bound has to be on the attempt — and on the part of it that is safe to redo.
- **29** — A path predicate written by SHAPE swallows the static siblings that share its prefix.
- **30** — A repository whose CI only runs on the trunk makes the trunk the first place anything is tested.
- **31** — A guard that asserts the MECHANISM makes the mechanism mandatory.
- **32** — A test that fails for the wrong reason conceals whether the right reason works.
- **33** — A catch-all registered under a framework's own defaults is not a catch-all.
- **34** — A guard written on a branch that never landed protects nothing, and its absence is silent.
- **35** — The one step that CANNOT be shared is the one that drifts — and a correct reason written beside a setting hides the second reason it is there.
- **36** — A hook that returns a fresh object or array is a loaded gun; the shot is fired in another file, on another day, by somebody who never saw it.
- **37** — Reading the code cannot find a performance bug; the profiler finds it in one step.
- **38** — An existence check that any RELATIVE can satisfy.
- **39** — A bad value that does not throw, and then serializes to something legal.
- **40** — Two conditions that are each correct can still be wrong about each other. A condition nested inside an unrelated one inherits its answer — and every unit test passes, because no unit is wrong.
- **41** — A new file's NAME is a claim that nothing already owns it, and writing one makes that claim silently.
- **42** — A test can fail AFTER it has passed, and the file it lands on is arbitrary.
- **43** — A test can be flaky BY CONSTRUCTION: a fixture that is random, mutated by a rule that does not guarantee a change.
- **44** — A test that kills what it spawned on its last line has no teardown at all — it has a happy path.
- **45** — Deduplicating by a key that is finer than the thing being deduplicated.
- **46** — New chrome takes its room from a shared budget, so it silently moves the threshold where OTHER chrome disappears — and anything hidden as a pair disappears together.
- **47** — The instrument answers cheerfully too.
- **48** — A translucent surface has no colour of its own, so any opaque state drawn ON it is a coin flip.
- **49** — A committed generated file depends on the wall clock.
- **50** — A snapshot read and a log tip taken at different moments leave a window that neither covers.
- **51** — A selftest's mutation can move the number for the wrong reason, and then it proves the wrong claim.
- **52** — A notice that arrives under a green status is read as the status.
- **53** — Two requests fired in the same tick race for a recovery that only one of them can win — and the one that is allowed to fail quietly is the one that dies.
